title: Meta’s Muse launches on iPad just a month after its mobile debut
key_facts: On Wednesday (7 Oct 2026) Meta announced a dedicated iPad app for Muse, its AI assistant.
Muse launched on iOS and Android on 8 Sep 2026 and has topped 6.6 million installs, according to estimates from Sensor Tower, a market intelligence firm.

Muse uses 'connectors' to outside services, which users sign into one by one; the iPad update adds Asana, Canva, Dropbox, Figma, QuickBooks, GitHub, Klaviyo, Zoom, Notion, Granola and Meta ad accounts.
Retail partners Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Walmart and Wayfair let the agent shop and complete transactions on their sites.
Meta said on Tuesday (6 Oct) it is working with industry partners on an open standard so AI agents can identify themselves to businesses.
The article says websites sometimes mistake agents for bots and block them, so these experiences can fail.
quote_evidence: Since launching on iOS and Android on September 8, Muse has topped 6.6 million installs, according to estimates from market intelligence firm Sensor Tower.
Because this technology is still new, these experiences can still run into issues as websites mistake agents for bots and block their access.
why_it_matters_hint: People who give an AI agent access to email, bookings and shopping; agent shopping can fail when sites block agents.
